introduction: Bassanio needs money to court Portia, an heiress whose father's will controls her choice of husband. His friend Antonio offers his credit, bringing them into a bargain with Shylock, a Jewish lender whom Antonio has repeatedly insulted. In Venice, commercial promises carry personal grievances; in Belmont, marriage depends on interpreting a test of appearances. The two worlds become linked by obligations that ask how much friendship, love, and an insistence on exact terms can demand from another person.

fullSynopsis.text: Bassanio hopes to repair his fortunes by winning Portia and asks Antonio for support. With his capital invested in ships abroad, Antonio offers his credit. Shylock agrees to lend three thousand ducats for three months, secured by Antonio's bond. He resents Antonio's attacks on Jewish people, his personal humiliations, and his interest-free lending. Antonio confirms that he may insult him again. Shylock presents a pound of Antonio's flesh as a playful penalty for default; Antonio accepts, expecting his ships before the debt matures, despite Bassanio's misgivings. At Belmont Portia must marry the suitor who chooses the casket containing her portrait.

Morocco chooses gold, believing it appropriate to the prize desired by everyone, and finds a death's head instead. Arragon chooses silver according to his estimate of his own deserts and receives a fool's portrait. Both depart bound by the conditions of the test. Meanwhile Launcelet leaves Shylock's service for Bassanio's. Shylock's daughter Jessica arranges to escape with Lorenzo, taking money and jewels from her father's house and disguising herself as a boy. She intends to become a Christian and Lorenzo's wife. Reports of Shylock's distress mingle with the first anxious news of lost ships that may belong to Antonio.

Shylock vows revenge on Antonio and defends Jewish humanity against Christian contempt, treating retaliation as something his enemies have taught him. Tubal alternately brings news of Antonio's losses and Jessica's spending, including the exchange of a ring Shylock received from Leah. At Belmont Bassanio rejects deceptive outward splendor and chooses lead, finding Portia's portrait. She gives herself and her household to him with a ring he must never surrender. Gratiano announces his matching engagement to Nerissa. News then arrives that Antonio's ventures have failed and Shylock demands the bond. Portia supplies money and sends Bassanio to Venice immediately after their marriage.

Shylock refuses Antonio's pleas. Portia entrusts Belmont to Lorenzo and Jessica, pretends to retire to a monastery, and secretly obtains legal notes and male clothing from her cousin Bellario. In court she appears as the young lawyer Balthazar, with Nerissa as clerk. Her appeal to mercy fails to move Shylock, who rejects repayment and insists on the flesh. Portia first upholds the bond, then rules that it permits no blood and exactly one pound, making its execution impossible without fatal penalties. She next invokes a law against an outsider seeking a citizen's life, exposing Shylock to forfeiture and the Duke's judgment.

The Duke spares Shylock's life. Antonio asks that the state's financial penalty be waived and that his own awarded half be held for Lorenzo after Shylock's death. He also demands Shylock's conversion to Christianity and a deed leaving what he possesses at death to Jessica and Lorenzo. The Duke makes compliance a condition of pardon. Shylock submits and leaves ill. Still disguised, Portia refuses money but asks Bassanio for his ring. He initially refuses, then sends it after her at Antonio's urging. Nerissa similarly obtains Gratiano's ring, allowing both women to test the promises their husbands have just broken.

At moonlit Belmont, Lorenzo and Jessica trade stories of lovers and listen to music before the returning couples reunite. Portia and Nerissa accuse their husbands over the missing rings and teasingly suggest that the lawyer and clerk have become their lovers. Antonio again offers himself as surety for Bassanio's fidelity. The women return the rings and reveal their disguises, resolving the apparent betrayal. Portia gives Antonio a letter reporting three ships safely arrived, restoring his livelihood as well as his life. Jessica and Lorenzo receive Shylock's deed of future inheritance. The company goes indoors for further explanation as Gratiano resolves to guard Nerissa's ring.

acts.label: ACT I
acts.summary: Antonio cannot explain his sadness but readily offers assistance when Bassanio describes his debts and hope of courting Portia. His available wealth is at sea, so he puts his credit at Bassanio's disposal. At Belmont, Portia complains that her father's casket test prevents her choosing a husband, reviews unwanted suitors with Nerissa, and remembers Bassanio favorably. Shylock negotiates a loan of three thousand ducats secured by Antonio. His private resentment concerns religion, Antonio's insults, and the damage free lending does to his business. Antonio refuses friendship and acknowledges that he may continue the abuse. Shylock nevertheless offers an interest-free bond with a pound of flesh as the penalty for failure to repay. Confident in his expected returns, Antonio accepts against Bassanio's objections.

acts.label: ACT II
acts.summary: Morocco agrees to the casket test's conditions, then chooses gold and fails. Arragon later chooses silver and also fails, leaving Portia free from both suits. In Venice Launcelet jokes with his nearly blind father before securing a place with Bassanio, and Gratiano gains leave to accompany his friend to Belmont. Jessica uses Launcelet to send Lorenzo instructions for her escape. While Shylock dines away from home, she leaves dressed as a boy, carrying his wealth, and joins Lorenzo. Bassanio sails that night. Salarino and Solanio report Shylock's anger and grief in hostile terms, discuss a possible shipwreck affecting Antonio, and describe Antonio's affectionate parting from Bassanio. At Belmont a new Venetian arrival brings gifts ahead of a suitor, raising hope that Bassanio is coming.

acts.label: ACT III
acts.summary: Reports of Antonio's losses strengthen Shylock's determination to claim the bond. He answers Christian mockery with an assertion of shared human feelings and a vow to imitate the revenge his enemies practice. Tubal's account of Jessica's spending hurts him, especially the loss of Leah's ring. At Belmont a song about desire accompanies Bassanio's rejection of ornament and choice of lead. Finding Portia's portrait, he wins her and receives a ring pledged as a permanent token. Gratiano and Nerissa also plan marriage. Antonio's letter interrupts the celebration with news of default. Portia provides funds and sends Bassanio to him, then secretly arranges a legal disguise while leaving Lorenzo and Jessica in charge. Antonio faces an unyielding Shylock, and Jessica defends her conversion in banter with Launcelet.

acts.label: ACT IV
acts.summary: Shylock rejects money and mercy in court, demanding the flesh. Portia, disguised as Balthazar and supported by Bellario's letter, first acknowledges the bond and appeals to compassion. When Shylock insists, she restricts him to exactly a pound without blood, then invokes penalties for attempting a Venetian citizen's life. The Duke pardons his life; Antonio proposes financial concessions tied to holding his awarded half for Lorenzo, Shylock's conversion, and a deed securing Jessica and Lorenzo's eventual inheritance. Under threat of losing the pardon, Shylock agrees. Portia refuses a fee but demands Bassanio's ring. Antonio persuades him to surrender it, and Gratiano delivers it. Nerissa plans to obtain her husband's ring while carrying the deed for Shylock to sign.

acts.label: ACT V
acts.summary: Lorenzo and Jessica exchange moonlit recollections of famous lovers, and music gives their waiting at Belmont a language of harmony. Portia and Nerissa arrive ahead of their husbands and ask that their absence be concealed. When Bassanio, Gratiano, and Antonio return, the women challenge the surrender of the rings and pretend to suspect sexual betrayal. The men explain their gratitude to the lawyer and clerk; Antonio offers a renewed guarantee of Bassanio's faith. Portia restores the rings and reveals that she and Nerissa themselves played those parts. A letter brings Antonio news of three ships safely returned, while Nerissa gives Jessica and Lorenzo the deed of future inheritance. They go indoors to hear the complete account, and Gratiano promises vigilance over his ring.
